title: PATENT RESEARCH REPORT
abstract: This technical report synthesizes polymerization and process parameters for Low Acrylonitrile Nitrile Butadiene Rubber (Low ACN NBR) based on a selected portfolio of six patents published between 2011 and 2017. Low ACN NBR (typically containing 27% to 36% bound acrylonitrile) is highly valued for its low-temperature flexibility and oil resistance. The analyzed patent landscape demonstrates that cold emulsion polymerization conducted at 7% to 8%C is the dominant industrial approach to synthesize these copolymers. Key process trends include the use of advanced redox initiator systems (such as diisopropylbenzene hydroperoxide or p-menthane hydroperoxide coupled with iron(II) salts and reducing agents like sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate or Rongalit C) to achieve high conversion (70% to 90%) within 6 to 7 hours. Molecular weight and Mooney viscosity are tightly regulated using tertiary dodecyl mercaptan (t-DDM) or tert-dodecyl mercaptan (TDM), often employing incremental booster additions during the reaction. Furthermore, post-polymerization coagulation conditions—specifically the choice of salt (MgCl2, CaCl2, MgSO4, or NaCl) and precise pH adjustment prior to coagulation—are shown to be critical in controlling the polymer's ion index, which directly dictates vulcanization kinetics, Mooney scorch safety, and final mechanical properties.

patent_details.patent_title: Process for the preparation of nitrile rubbers
patent_details.assignee: Not disclosed in the analyzed patent evidence.
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses a low-temperature emulsion polymerization process for NBR with low-to-medium bound ACN content (27.9% to 33.9%) utilizing incremental chain-transfer agent additions.

polymerization_method.monomer_ratio: Latex A: 500 g acrylonitrile and 4.37 kg butadiene (~10.3% ACN in feed). Latex B: 815 g acrylonitrile and 4.0 kg butadiene (~16.9% ACN in feed).
polymerization_method.emulsifier: Potassium stearate and potassium salt of disproportionated rosin acid (DNMK).
polymerization_method.emulsifier_loading: 0.53 kg of 5.4% wt aqueous potassium stearate solution and 0.440 kg of DNMK.
polymerization_method.catalyst_activator: Sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate (FSS) (139 g of aqueous solution).
polymerization_method.chain_transfer_dosage: 18.72 g initially (for Latex A), with subsequent booster additions of 2.34 g at 37% and 59% conversion.
polymerization_method.pressure: Not disclosed in the analyzed patent evidence.
polymerization_method.ph: 8.5 to 8.6 (latex pH before coagulation); coagulation pH adjusted to 11.5-11.8.
polymerization_method.coagulation_conditions: Latex (10 kg) added over 10 minutes to a mixture of 43 kg water and 4 kg saturated magnesium sulfate solution at 45%C, with pH adjusted to 11.5-11.8 using potassium hydroxide (14 g).
polymerization_method.post_treatment: Crumbs (1.5 kg) filtered, washed with deionized water, and dried in an air oven at 100%C for 24 hours to a residual humidity of less than 1%.
polymerization_method.raw_polymer_properties: Latex A: Bound ACN 28.1%, Mooney Viscosity 60.5 MU. Latex B: Bound ACN 33.9%, Mooney Viscosity 32.1 MU. Latex C: Bound ACN 27.9%, Mooney Viscosity 29.0 MU.

experimental_evidence: Latex A was prepared by charging 9.92 kg deionized water, potassium stearate, and DNMK, followed by vacuum application and charging 500 g ACN, 18.72 g TDM, and 4.37 kg butadiene.
Polymerization was initiated at 7%C by injecting 6 g DIHP and 139 g FSS solution.
TDM boosters (2.34 g each) were added at 37% and 59% conversion to control molecular weight.
Reaction was shortstopped at 70% conversion using 515 g of 2% wt hydroxylamine sulfate solution.
Latex was stabilized with 1% wt BHT antioxidant dispersion before being coagulated with magnesium sulfate at pH 11.5-11.8.
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: Demonstrates that split-addition of TDM chain transfer agent during cold emulsion polymerization successfully controls Mooney viscosity in low-ACN nitrile rubbers.

Corrosion testing of sealing rings was conducted at 80% relative humidity and 70%C between aluminum plates.

experimental_evidence: Nitrile rubbers were processed in a 1.5 L mechanical laboratory mixer with compounding ingredients reported in parts per 100 parts of rubber.
Vulcanization kinetics were measured according to DIN 53 529, part 3, identifying t10 and t90 times.
Coagulation with magnesium chloride resulted in lower Mooney scorch, shorter vulcanization times, and higher stress at 300% elongation compared to calcium chloride coagulation.
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: Establishes that magnesium chloride coagulation optimizes vulcanization rates and enhances tensile stress at high elongation for NBR.

patent_details.assignee: Not disclosed in the analyzed patent evidence.
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses a highly detailed emulsion polymerization recipe for nitrile rubbers containing low-to-medium ACN (35-36%) using specific redox catalyst systems.

polymerization_method.monomer_ratio: 61.4 parts butadiene, 36 parts acrylonitrile, and 2.6 parts 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate.
polymerization_method.water_amount: 220 parts by weight per 100 parts monomer (total water in autoclave: 2.1 kg).
polymerization_method.emulsifier_loading: 3.0 parts by weight per 100 parts monomer.
polymerization_method.initiator: P-menthane hydroperoxide (Trigonox NT 50) and Fe(II)SO4*7H2O or Fe(II)Cl2*4H2O.
polymerization_method.initiator_loading: 0.02 parts by weight Trigonox NT 50; 0.030 parts by weight Fe(II) salt premix.
polymerization_method.catalyst_activator: Rongalit C (2.0 g) and EDTA in an equimolar amount relative to Fe(II).
polymerization_method.chain_transfer_dosage: 0.54 parts by weight per 100 parts monomer.
polymerization_method.pressure: 50 bar to 150 bar (for subsequent hydrogenation steps, if applicable).
polymerization_method.coagulation_conditions: Latex admixed with a 50% dispersion of Vulkanox BKF (0.3% wt based on NBR solids) prior to coagulation.
polymerization_method.post_treatment: Shortstopped with diethylhydroxylamine (0.2 parts), stabilized with Wingstay 29/Naugawhite antioxidant mixture, and coagulated.
polymerization_method.raw_polymer_properties: ACN content: 35.3% - 36.6%. Mooney viscosity: 25 - 142 MU. Glass transition temperature (Tg): -23.1%C to -25.8%C.

experimental_evidence: Autoclave batches utilized 1.25 kg monomer mixture and 2.1 kg water.
Premix solution contained 0.986 g Fe(II)SO4*7H2O or 0.845 g Fe(II)Cl2*4H2O and 2.0 g Rongalit C in 400 g water.
Polymerization of Rubber G (FeSO4 premix) reached 86.1% conversion in 7.0 hours; Rubber H (FeCl2 premix) reached 84.2% conversion in 6.5 hours.
Antioxidant stabilization was performed using a mixture of Sorbilene Mix (25 g), Naugawhite (38 g), Wingstay 29 (125 g), and water (63 g).
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: Provides a precise, reproducible cold emulsion polymerization recipe demonstrating that specific Fe(II) redox systems control branching and Mooney viscosity in low-to-medium ACN rubbers.

experimental_evidence: Latex pH was adjusted to 9.5 or 8.4 using 5% KOH, or to 5.8 using 5% HCl before coagulation.
Coagulation trials compared NaCl (15-26% wt) and CaCl2 (0.3-1.2% wt) at temperatures from 20%C to 50%C.
Nitrile rubbers with optimized ion indices exhibited significantly higher vulcanization rates (t90 - t10) and higher stress values at 30% elongation.
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: Demonstrates that pre-coagulation pH adjustment and salt selection are critical process controls to regulate the ion index and enhance vulcanization kinetics.
